extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians / natural philosophers (readers of Newton's Principia), Latin-literate scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and records the principal lemmas, corollaries and propositions in Newton's Latin Principia Livre I (sections on method, lemmata, and first proposition) that state geometric-method rules and physical laws about motion, collisions, centres of gravity, and central forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. III: Quantitas motus non mutatur ab actione corporum inter se
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitas motus quæ colligitur capiendo summam motuum factorum ad eandem partem, & differentiam factorum ad contrarias, non mutatur ab actione corporum inter se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of conservation of the total quantity of motion (momentum) for interacting bodies. Includes worked numerical examples of collisions (spherical bodies A and B with various ratios of masses and velocity parts) showing that the sum of motions directed one way plus difference directed the other remains constant (examples: sums of parts like 16 preserved; specific post-collision velocity-part arithmetic is shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. IV: Commune centrum gravitatis statum suum non mutat ab actionibus internis
rubrics_metrics.description: Commune gravitatis centrum ab actionibus corporum inter se non mutat statum suum vel motus vel quietis, & propterea corporum omnium in se mutuo agentium (exclusis actionibus & impedimentis externis) commune centrum gravitatis vel quiescit vel movetur uniformiter in directum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement that the center of gravity of a system is unaffected by internal forces — it either remains at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line. The text gives a geometric argument by induction on numbers of bodies and explains consequences for systems and single bodies: motion of system assessed by motion of its centre of gravity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. V: Motus relativi invariantes sub translatione uniformi
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporum dato spatio inclusorum ijdem sunt motus inter se, sive spatium illud quiescat, sive moveatur idem uniformiter in directum absq; motu circulari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of Galilean relativity: motions of bodies relative to one another are unchanged if the whole space is translated uniformly. The corollary is supported by argument from equality of relative motions and an experimental note (ship example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. VI: Equal parallel accelerations do not change relative motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpora moveantur quomodocunq; inter se & a viribus acceleratricibus æqualibus secundum lineas parallelas urgeantur; pergent omnia eodem modo moveri inter se ac si viribus illis non essent incitata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all bodies are uniformly accelerated by equal forces along parallel lines, their mutual motions are unaffected: the added identical acceleration cancels out for relative motion. The brief geometric justification appeals to Law II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on experimental confirmation and elasticity (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hactenus principia tradidi ... Per leges duas primas & Corollaria duo prima adinvenit Galilæus descensum gravium esse in duplicata ratione temporis ... Et ut hoc experimentum cum Theorijs ad amussim congruat, habenda est ratio tum resistentiæ aeris, tum etiam vis Elasticæ concurrentium corporum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative summarising experimental confirmations (Galileo on free fall and projectiles, pendulum experiments) and introducing experimental corrections: method to measure and correct for air resistance in pendulum experiments (construct semicircles, measure retardations RV etc.). Also discusses elasticity in collisions: perfectly elastic bodies rebound with relative velocity equal to incident; imperfect elasticity reduces rebound velocity determinably. Gives observed approximate rebound ratios for woolen balls (~5:9), steel, cork, glass (~15:16). Includes practical experimental procedure for approximating vacuum behaviour by correcting pendulum amplitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma I: Limits of quantities whose ratios approach equality are equal
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitates, ut & quantitatum rationes, quæ ad æqualitatem dato tempore constanter tendunt & eo pacto propius ad invicem accedere possunt quam pro data quavis differentia; fiunt ultimo æquales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological lemma about limits: if two quantities (or their ratios) can be made arbitrarily close, their ultimate (limit) ratios are equal. Used to justify arguments by evanescent (vanishing) quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma II: Inscribed and circumscribed parallelogram approximations converge to same area
rubrics_metrics.description: Si in figura quavis ... inscribantur parallelogramma quotcunq; ... dein latitudo minuatur, & numerus augeatur in infinitum: dico quod ultimæ rationes, quas habent ad se invicem figura inscripta AKbLcMdD, circumscripta AalbmcndoE, & curvilinea AabcdE, sunt rationes æqualitatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric lemma establishing that inscribed and circumscribed polygonal approximations to a curved figure have equal ultimate ratios (basis for area by limits). Uses subdividing into parallelograms and Lemma I to take limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma III: Same conclusion when strip-widths are unequal
rubrics_metrics.description: Eædem rationes ultimæ sunt etiam æqualitatis, ubi parallelogrammorum latitudines AB, BC, CD, &c. sunt inæquales, & omnes minuuntur in infinitum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variant of Lemma II allowing unequal widths that nevertheless diminish to zero; corollaries: sum of vanishing parallelograms coincides with the curvilinear figure; rectilinear figures defined by chords or tangents coincide in the limit with the curvilinear figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma IV: Ratio of figures from equal-series-of-parallelograms
rubrics_metrics.description: Si in duabus figuris AacE, PprT, inscribantur (ut supra) duæ parallelogrammorum series, sitq; idem amborum numerus, & ubi latitudines in infinitum diminuitur, rationes ultimæ parallelogrammorum in una figura ad parallelogramma in altera, singulorum ad singula, sint eædem; dico quod figuræ duæ AacE, PprT, sunt ad invicem in eadem illa ratione.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that if corresponding infinitesimal parallelogram elements are in a given ratio, the entire figures are in that ratio (sums/limits preserve ratios). Useful for comparing areas/figures by elemental ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma V: Similar figures have proportional corresponding sides; areas in duplicate ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Similium figurarum latera omnia, quæ sibi mutuo respondent, sunt proportionalia, tam curvilinea quam rectilinea, & areæ sunt in duplicata ratione laterum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard similarity result extended to curvilinear figures: corresponding sides proportional and areas scale as square of side ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma VI: Angle between chord and tangent vanishes as points coalesce
rubrics_metrics.description: Si arcus quilibet positione datus AB subtendatur chorda AB, & in puncto aliquo A, in medio curvaturæ continuæ, tangatur a recta utrinq; producta AD; dein puncta A, B ad invicem accedant & coeant; dico quod angulus BAD sub chorda & tangente contentus minuetur in infinitum & ultimo evanescet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric small-angle result: as the chord endpoint approaches the tangent point, angle between chord and tangent tends to zero. Used to justify replacing small arcs by chords/tangents in limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma VII: Ultimate ratio of arc, chord and tangent is equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis, dico quod ultima ratio arcus, chordæ & tangentis ad invicem est ratio æqualitatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of Lemma VI: in the limit the measures of arc, chord and tangent coincide in ratio — allows interchange in limit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma VIII: Limiting triangles are similar
rubrics_metrics.description: Si rectæ datæ AR, BR cum arcu AB, chorda AB & tangente AD, triangula tria ARB, ARB, ARD constituunt, dein puncta A, B accedunt ad invicem: dico quod ultima forma triangulorum evanescentium est similitudinis, & ultima ratio æqualitatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows triangles formed with chords/tangents approach similarity in the limit; used to transfer proportionality relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma IX: Areas of triangles with ordinates in duplicate ratio of sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Si recta AE & Curva AC positione datæ se mutuo secent in angulo dato A, & ad rectam illam in alio dato angulo ordinatim applicentur BD, EC, curvæ occurrentes in B, C; dein puncta B, C accedant ad punctum A: dico quod areæ triangulorum ADB, AEC erunt ultimo ad invicem in duplicata ratione laterum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that curvilinear-triangle areas formed by ordinates behave in the limit as the square of the sides (duplicate ratio), underpinning area ~ side^2 relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma X: Distances under regular force are in duplicate ratio of times
rubrics_metrics.description: Spatia, quæ corpus urgente quacunq; vi regulari describit, sunt ipso motus initio in duplicata ratione temporum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kinematic lemma: for motion under any regularly applied force (i.e., with certain regularity), distances from the start are proportional to the squares of the times (i.e., s ~ t^2 initially). Corollaries note that errors from similar bodies under similar applied forces scale as squares of times and as forces times square-times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XI: Small-angle chord/tangent subtension relation (quadratic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtensa evanescens anguli contactus est ultimo in ratione duplicata subtensæ arcus contermini.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates small-angle contact-lengths: in the limit the subtended perpendicular from tangent (contact) is in the duplicate (square) ratio of the subtended arc. Several corollaries follow relating triangle areas and parabolic segment areas in triple/compound ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on method of limits vs indivisibles (methodological guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cæterum in his omnibus supponimus angulum contactus nec infinite majorem esse ... Neq; novit natura limitem. ... Præmisi vero hæc Lemmata ut effugerem tædium deducendi perplexas demonstrationes, more veterum Geometrarum, ad absurdum. Contractiores enim redduntur demonstrationes per methodum indivisibilium. Sed quoniam durior est indivisibilium Hypothesis; & propterea Methodus illa minus Geometrica censetur, malui demonstrationes rerum sequentium ad ultimas quantitatum evanescentium summas & rationes, primasq; nascentium, id est, ad limites summarum & rationum deducere, & propterea limitum illorum demonstrationes qua potui breuitate præmittere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological prescription: use limits (ultimate ratios of evanescent quantities) rather than indivisibles; treat infinitesimal arguments as limits. Clarifies how to interpret 'ultima ratio' and 'velocitas ultima'. Provides rebuttals to objections about indivisibles and infinite processes. Guidance to read evanescent quantities as diminishing without bound, and ultimate/first ratios as limits at the moment of vanishing or arising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. I Theor. I: Areas swept by radius to center of force proportional to time
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas quas corpora in gyros acta radiis ad immobile centrum virium ductis describunt, & in planis immobilibus consistere, & esse temporibus proportionales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental theorem: for motion under a central force (centripetal), the sectorial areas swept out by the radius vector are proportional to the times taken (equal areas in equal times). Proof by discretizing time and showing triangles equal in equal times; passing to the limit yields curved area result. This is the geometric expression of conservation of angular momentum and is the basis for treating central-force motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries to Prop. I: Conditions on area-time proportionality and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Corol. 1. In mediis non resistentibus, si areæ non sunt temporibus proportionales, vires non tendunt ad concursum radiorum. Corol. 2. In mediis omnibus, si arearum descriptio acceleratur, vires non tendunt ad concursum radiorum, sed inde declinant in consequentia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 1: In non-resisting media, if areas swept are not proportional to times, the forces are not directed to a common center (i.e., not purely central). Corollary 2: In media with resistance, accelerating area-description indicates forces do not tend to concurrent radii and the center-of-force concept changes accordingly. These indicate diagnostic tests: check area-time proportionality to infer concurrency of centripetal forces.
